title: Vision AI for planograms: from nice-to-have to non-negotiable in 24 months. — Trackeys

hero.h1: Vision AI for planograms: from nice-to-have to non-negotiable in 24 months.
hero.p: Two years ago, AI shelf audits were a premium upsell. Today, they're table stakes. Here's why — and what makes a good vision model for retail execution.

sections.sub:
Three years ago, "AI merchandising" on an RFP meant a shelf-image-capture feature a human auditor would later review. Today, the bar is a real-time detection model that scores planogram compliance, share-of-shelf and out-of-stock on the rep's phone in under 3 seconds.
Two things: model quality got dramatically better for long-tail SKU detection, and phones got fast enough to run inference on-device. The result is that a rep walking into a 200-SKU aisle can get instant, objective compliance scoring — no more human audit queues, no more week-long feedback loops.
SKU-level recall above 94%. Sub-second inference on mid-tier Android devices. Handles edge cases — shelf occlusion, odd lighting, skewed angles — without collapsing confidence. And trained on your actual SKU catalog, not a generic CPG dataset.
